note: Mixolydian heard as major with one note lowered (modes:3): the 7th and the ♭7 tapped on two staffs, the ♭7 against a drone, then lines landing on it over a Mixolydian backing track, whose two chords are counted the long way once as chord tokens. The old Key choice is moves (any key), so the key is named only as {{=key}} and a {{?key}} line says the ringed note is still the ♭7.

exercise.title: Mixolydian: major with a lowered 7th
exercise.why: Mixolydian is the major scale with its 7th lowered a half step, so a line that leans on that ♭7 over the root sounds Mixolydian, and the rest of it sounds like major.

cells.text: The staff below shows the {{=key}} major scale: tap a note to hear it. Tap {{6}}, the ringed {{7}} and the {{1}} above them: a half step from {{7}} up to {{1}}.

This staff shows {{=key}} Mixolydian. Tap {{6}}, the ringed {{b7}} and {{1}}: now there is a whole step from {{b7}} up to {{1}}.
Go between the two staffs. Practice until you hear the lowered note coming before you tap it.

Press Play below to start the drone on {{1}}. Tap {{1}}, {{b7}} and {{1}} on the staff under it, then tap short lines of your own that keep coming back to {{b7}}.
If a line drifts away from the drone, end it on {{1}} and start the next one from {{b7}}.

{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}. {{chord:bVII}} is the chord built on {{b7}}.
Press Play below to start the backing track: four bars, with {{chord:I}} first and last. Tap lines of your own on the staff under it, and land on the ringed {{b7}} when {{chord:bVII}} comes: that note is its root.
Practice until the {{b7}} lands with the chord.
{{?key}}In another key the notes are new, and the ringed note is still the ♭7, the root of the second chord.
